title: When the Repo Rate Holds, WACC Still Moves
subtitle: RBI kept the policy repo at 5.25% in August 2026. A composite auto-ancillary CFO must still reset working-capital mix, capex timing, and the cost of equity before the board's September review.
category: Monetary Policy, Cost of Capital & CFO Judgment
description: HBS-style teaching case dated 9 September 2026. Publicly reported facts from RBI Monetary Policy Statement, 3–5 August 2026: MPC unanimously held the LAF repo at 5.25%; SDF 5.00%; MSF and Bank Rate 5.50%; stance remains neutral. Real GDP growth for 2026-27 projected at 6.7% (Q1 7.0; Q2 6.4; Q3 6.5; Q4 6.8). CPI inflation for 2026-27 projected at 5.0% (Q2 4.7; Q3 5.9; Q4 5.5). Headline CPI rose to 4.4% in June 2026 after 16 consecutive months below the 4% target. Inflation target of 4% +/- 2% retained for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031. GST e-way bills +12.4% and GST revenue +8.6% in Q1:2026-27. Composite firm: Godavari Precision Components Ltd. Composite decision-maker: CFO Meera Kulkarni.
thumbnail: REPO HELD AT 5.25%. WHY IS YOUR WACC STILL MOVING?
sources: Reserve Bank of India, Monetary Policy Statement 2026-27, Resolution of the Monetary Policy Committee, August 3 to 5, 2026. Repo unchanged at 5.25%; SDF 5.00%; MSF and Bank Rate 5.50%; stance neutral.
RBI, Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, August 3 to 5, 2026 (released 19 August 2026).
RBI press materials and Bulletin: real GDP 2026-27 projected 6.7%; CPI 2026-27 projected 5.0%; June 2026 CPI 4.4% after 16 months below target.
Government of India / RBI: inflation target of 4 per cent with a tolerance band of +/- 2 per cent retained for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031.
RBI high-frequency indicators cited in August 2026 policy: GST e-way bills +12.4% and GST revenue +8.6% in Q1:2026-27; manufacturing PMI 54.6 in Q1.
